recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-18088; future changes to severity definitions or binding semantics should be handled through their own tracker issues.
issue_request: FHIR-18088 was a Published Security WG change request, resolved Persuasive for R5, asking AuditEvent to add a severity element for Debug, Informational, Notice, Warning, and higher Syslog severity levels, with ATNA mapping to the SYSLOG PRI element.
initial_application: HL7/fhir PR #708, merged as e5f777ad514d570245abf181a3637f154a2529a9, implemented the request. Commit 8f93636e058fa1a4b9ce4240fea41076e10e6760 added AuditEvent.severity to the AuditEvent spreadsheet as a 0..1 code with a required AuditEventSeverity binding and SYSLOG PRI mapping, and e8660657fb334c6180816598e9ff668f2ba7e7e0 corrected the severity short display text. The 2021 source refactor in 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 carried the element into the current StructureDefinition XML source.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes AuditEvent, so source/auditevent/structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml and the adjacent AuditEvent terminology files are in current build scope. The current source defines AuditEvent.severity as 0..1 code, summary, with a required binding to ValueSet/audit-event-severity; the CodeSystem contains the eight Syslog-derived severity codes. Later FHIR-32442 clarified the AuditEventSeverity concept definitions and already has a combined-branch issue-reconcile commit, so it was treated as context rather than an additional decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active source already satisfies the final FHIR-18088 request by including AuditEvent.severity with the requested severity levels and SYSLOG PRI mapping. Changing the element to Coding would be broader than the applied R5 decision and would conflict with the established required code binding.
